pro_course_detail.title: Conversational English (All Levels)
pro_course_detail.description:
My Conversational English lessons are designed to help students of all proficiency levels—from beginners to experts—develop their speaking skills in a supportive and engaging environment.

Core Activities: 
Role-Playing: Simulate real-life scenarios (e.g., ordering food, job interviews, travel).
Discussion Circles: Group discussions on selected topics (e.g., hobbies, cultural differences).
Debate Sessions: Structured debates on controversial issues (e.g., environmental policies).
Storytelling: Students create and share stories based on prompts, enhancing creativity and fluency.
Conversation Games: Interactive games (e.g., “20 Questions,” “Would You Rather?”) to build vocabulary and spontaneity.

Material and Resources:
Articles and Short Stories: Authentic reading materials to stimulate discussion.
Videos and Podcasts: Multimedia resources to expose students to various accents and conversational styles.
Real-life Objects and Pictures: Visual aids to spark conversations and build descriptive language skills.

Each lesson is tailored to the students’ levels and needs, ensuring a balance between structured activities and free-flowing conversation. The goal is to build confidence, improve fluency, and make learning English an enjoyable and rewarding experience. Through varied activities, authentic materials, and diverse topics, students will find themselves more comfortable and proficient in conversational English.

pro_course_detail.title: English for Studying Abroad
pro_course_detail.description:
The "English for Studying Abroad" course is designed to equip students with the language skills and cultural knowledge needed to succeed in an academic setting abroad. The course will cover a range of levels, from beginner to advanced, ensuring that all students receive tailored instruction to meet their specific needs.

Beginner Level:
-Vocabulary building: Common academic terms, classroom objects, basic phrases.
Simple conversations: Introducing oneself, asking for directions, basic classroom interactions.
-Reading and comprehension: Short texts related to student life, simple articles.
-Listening exercises: Understanding classroom instructions, short dialogues.

Intermediate Level:
-Expanded vocabulary: Subject-specific terminology, idiomatic expressions.
-Group discussions: Participating in study groups, sharing opinions on academic topics.
-Reading and writing: Summarizing articles, writing short essays.
-Listening and speaking: Note-taking from lectures, presenting ideas in class.

Advanced Level:
-Advanced vocabulary: Academic research terms, professional jargon.
-Debates and presentations: Arguing a point of view, delivering structured presentations.
-In-depth reading: Analyzing journal articles, critical thinking exercises.
-Writing: Crafting research papers, composing formal emails.

By the end of this course, students will feel confident and prepared to navigate the academic challenges and cultural differences they will encounter while studying abroad.
